_comment: Sites where a synchronous std::process::Command is waited on with no
time bound, and that are ACCEPTED. Enforced by
'site' is '<repo-relative path>::<enclosing fn name>' — stable across
edits above and below the call, which a line number is not.
'sites' is how many blocking waits that function currently contains;
the checker fails if the real number differs in EITHER direction, so
the baseline can only shrink and cannot silently rot.
'reason' is REQUIRED and must say why an unbounded wait is acceptable
HERE — i.e. why this code is not on a periodic or hot path. An empty
reason fails the gate, so --update-baseline cannot smuggle in an
Do NOT add an entry to silence a periodic caller. Route it through

exemptions.reason: One-shot macOS `security find-generic-password` attribute query on the OAuth-refresh decision path, not a timer. It is a local Keychain read with no -w/-g, so it never prompts and never waits on a network or a lock.

Teardown path: `taskkill /F /T` against a pid we are already killing. It runs once per pi child at end-of-session, and blocking here is bounded by the OS's own terminate call rather than by the dead child.

This IS the 'run an AI CLI session to completion' primitive — a claude/pi run legitimately takes minutes to hours, so any wall-clock bound here would be wrong. Its lifetime is governed by the session's own cancellation, and it is one call per user-started session, never periodic.
Standalone CLI binary (`qontinui_cli`), not the runner. It has no tokio runtime and therefore no blocking pool to exhaust; the process is one command and exits.

The PATH shim's whole job is to become the real tool: it must inherit stdio and wait for exactly as long as the real `git`/`cargo` takes. A timeout here would truncate the very command the caller asked for. Separate binary, no tokio runtime.

Runs a user-authored check command (lint/typecheck/test) whose runtime is legitimately unbounded. The budget belongs to the check step's own configured timeout, not to a blanket wrapper here. Invoked per user-started check run, never on a timer.
Tauri command — fires on a user opening the instances view. `git worktree list --porcelain` is a local plumbing read against an already-open repo.
One-shot macOS Keychain attribute query inside `coord doctor`, an operator-invoked diagnostic. Attribute-only (no -w/-g), so it never prompts.
Tauri command: the operator clicked 'force stop' on a specific pid. `taskkill /F /T` on a named pid, once per click.
Drain is an explicit operator/shutdown action, not a timer. Its git calls are local plumbing reads inside a repo the drain already resolved.
User-requested stop of a task run: `taskkill /F /T` once per tracked AI pid, on the stop path only.
Process shutdown. The taskkill loop reaps orphaned AI children as the runner exits; there is no later tick that could leak a thread, and the runtime is being torn down anyway.
User/agent-requested stop of an AI analysis: `taskkill /F /T` once per tracked pid, on the stop path only.
`cargo --version` behind a `Lazy` — it runs at most ONCE per process lifetime and the result is cached forever. Not a periodic caller by construction.
`mypy --version` / `python -m mypy --version` behind a `Lazy` — at most once per process, cached forever.
`tsc --version` resolution for a typecheck scope. Runs on the operator/agent-initiated typecheck path, not a timer, and only after `find_tsc` has already located the binary on disk.
Failure path only: the headless browser did not connect within its own timeout, so we `taskkill` the pid we just spawned. Reached once per failed spawn, on an agent-initiated request.
User/agent-requested stop of a task run: `taskkill /F /T` once per tracked AI pid, on the stop path only.
One ffmpeg frame-extraction pass per verification request, bounded by `-frames:v`. Agent-initiated, never on a timer; a transcode of a long trace legitimately takes minutes.
Runs the workspace's own `npm run build` / equivalent — an unbounded build by nature, and the point of the check is to let it finish. One pass per agent-initiated verification request.

Executes a user-authored orchestrator hook command. Its runtime is whatever the operator's script does; a blanket budget here would silently truncate hooks. Fires per task-run lifecycle event, not on a timer.

Executes a user-authored verification command (build/test/lint) whose runtime is legitimately unbounded. Budget belongs to the verification step's own config. One pass per orchestrator iteration, driven by task progress rather than a clock.
Runs a Playwright test script; a browser test legitimately runs for minutes and already carries its own `timeout_ms`. User/agent-initiated per run, never periodic.
Same as `run_script`, for the inline-script form: the Playwright run owns its own timeout and is user/agent-initiated per run.

`<pm> --version` with stdout/stderr nulled, used to detect which package manager exists. Called only from the detection routine in this module, whose result callers cache; it is startup/first-use work, not a tick.
`profile_cli` is a standalone operator CLI for editing the user PATH. No tokio runtime, no blocking pool; the process runs one command and exits.
Same as `read_path_scope`: standalone operator CLI, no tokio runtime, one command per process.
`where.exe git` fallback, reached only when none of the well-known bash.exe paths exist. `where.exe` is a local PATH scan; the call happens while preparing a user-authored shell step, not on a timer.
`tasklist` filtered to chrome.exe, run while assembling a diagnostics report after a failed test. Operator/agent-initiated, one pass per report.
Runs `npx playwright test`; the run carries its own `timeout_ms` and legitimately takes minutes. One invocation per user/agent-started test run.
Runs a user-authored python test script whose runtime is unbounded by design. One invocation per user/agent-started test run.
Runs the repo's own configured test command — unbounded by nature, and the budget belongs to the test config. One invocation per user/agent-started run.
User-triggered window activation (`wmctrl`/`xdotool`), one pass per click. Local X11 clients that return in milliseconds or fail immediately when no display is present.
User-triggered window activation via `osascript`, one pass per click.
User-triggered window enumeration (`wmctrl -l -p`, `xdotool search`), one pass per click on the window picker.
User-triggered window enumeration via `osascript`, one pass per click on the window picker.
Per-window `xdotool getwindowpid` / `getwindowname` follow-ups inside the user-triggered enumeration above; same one-pass-per-click lifetime.
`node --version` with stdio nulled — a fail-fast startup precondition check for the wrapper install pipeline, run once before installs rather than on a schedule.
